runs.question: Which four functions make up the NIST AI RMF Core, and which one is described as cross-cutting?

answer.text:
The AI RMF Core has four functions: GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE. The Core is composed of four functions: GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE.

GOVERN is the cross-cutting one. The framework presents it as something that feeds into the other three rather than a stage of its own. Governance is designed to be a cross-cutting function to inform and be infused throughout the other three functions. The framework also notes that GOVERN covers the whole risk management process, while the other three can be applied to specific AI systems and lifecycle stages. While GOVERN applies to all stages of organizations' AI risk management processes and procedures, the MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE functions can be applied in AI system-specific contexts and at specific stages of the AI lifecycle.
